title: Broker (Pub/Sub)
description: Fire-and-forget Redis pub/sub primitive and cross-process job events

blocks.text: The Broker is a generic Redis pub/sub primitive — fire-and-forget fan-out, deliberately separate from Hound's durable job execution. They solve different problems and do not overlap:

rows: Live UI updates, cache busts, signals

blocks.text: Rule of thumb: if a missed message matters, it's a job — use Hound. If a missed message is irrelevant the moment the listener is gone (a disconnected dashboard doesn't need the update), it's an event — use the Broker.

One Broker instance owns the subscriber dispatcher and a ref-counted channel registry: the first listener on a channel subscribes it on Redis, the last one leaving unsubscribes it. With ioredis, pass the main connection as pub — the subscriber connection is derived via duplicate(), since a Redis connection in subscriber mode cannot run normal commands:
Domain wrappers stay tiny — encode the channel scheme once and export named helpers:
publish() swallows serialization and transport errors by design — it must never poison the code path that called it. If you need confirmation of delivery, you wanted a job, not an event.

Job-finished notifications (emitAndWait, management.events, the gateway's /events stream) are in-process by default: the worker that ran the job is the one that notifies. When your gateway and workers are different processes or machines, pass a Broker to Hound on both sides — terminal job events are then published to the hound:job.finished channel and consumed from it:

items: emitAndWait() on the gateway box resolves when a worker box completes the job
GET /events streams completions from every worker, not just the local one
Jobs dead-lettered by the Reaper (poison cutoff) are announced too
Events you published yourself are not re-delivered locally — each instance tags its messages with an origin id and skips its own echoes

blocks.text: The channel name is exported as JOB_FINISHED_CHANNEL if you want to subscribe to job events directly from non-Hound code.
